44bcbb4f0bb6ca3ca6a74be91d08b24172bf76b0.summary: The report, published by The Hacker News on 2025-04-02, describes FIN7, a financially motivated Russian cybercrime group, as linked to Anubis, a Python-based backdoor that gives remote access to compromised Windows systems. PRODAFT, a Swiss security company, is quoted on the malware's ability to give attackers full control. Anubis is believed to be spread through malspam that entices victims to run a payload hosted on compromised SharePoint sites. GDATA, a German security company, reported that the backdoor can run operator-provided responses as shell commands. The report also says that in…

hedges: FIN7 has been linked to the Anubis backdoor; the report does not state the attribution's source beyond the article.
Anubis is believed to be propagated via malspam campaigns.
The threat actor is said to have transitioned to a ransomware affiliate.
The AuKill tool is advertised in a likely attempt to diversify its monetization strategy.
The backdoor is kept lightweight to reduce the risk of detection, per PRODAFT's description.

44528d153681a19a67e9f595deaeaf3dff38e485.summary: WithSecure Intelligence reports attacks in late March 2023 against internet-facing Veeam Backup & Replication servers. The intrusion set overlaps with FIN7, or with a threat actor using FIN7 tradecraft. Initial access is likely via CVE-2023-27532, a low-to-medium confidence assessment. The attackers ran PowerShell loaders (POWERTRASH) that delivered DICELOADER (also known as Lizar), then gathered credentials and host information, moved laterally, and set up persistence through POWERHOLD and DUBLOADER. Two instances were identified. The goal was unclear because the attacks were mitigated…

subject.name: FIN7 tradecraft attacks against Veeam backup servers

hedges: Initial access via the Veeam vulnerability is a low-to-medium confidence assessment, as no concrete indicators confirm it.
The exact method used to invoke the initial shell commands remains unknown.
Attribution was broadened from FIN7 to FIN7 or a threat actor utilizing FIN7 tradecraft in a 2023 update.
The earlier 24th March 2023 activity is not strongly linked to the intrusions and its reason remains unknown.
The goal of the attacks was unclear at the time of writing, as they were mitigated before fully materializing.
The payload of the final stage is believed likely to be a Cobalt Strike beacon, but its full contents could not be fetched.
The scope of the attack is believed to be limited given the probable rarity of publicly exposed port 9401.
